filename: Resolving Low Cloud Feedbacks Globally With E3SM High-Res MMF_ Agreement With LES but Stronger Shortwave Effects.pdf
title: Resolving Low Cloud Feedbacks Globally With E3SM High-Res MMF: Agreement With LES but Stronger Shortwave Effects
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
testbed_rationale: Provides open 5-year global simulation datasets resolving small-scale boundary-layer eddies and low cloud updrafts at 200 m CRM grid resolution under both present and warmed (+4 K) climate states, suitable as a reference benchmark for developing and evaluating ML-based cloud parameterizations.
pain_points: High computational cost requiring GPU-accelerated supercomputing for multi-year CRM-resolving runs.
Storage limitations restricted high-frequency output and required offline estimation of downward longwave radiation profiles at cloud top.
2D CRM geometry and 200 m horizontal grid spacing do not fully resolve sharp inversion-scale entrainment compared to 3D fine-scale LES.
Historical MMF low cloud under-representation required extensive physical tuning of hyperviscosity, droplet sedimentation, and autoconversion thresholds.
Uniform SST +4 K warming omits SST pattern effects, interactive aerosols, and direct CO2 radiative forcing.
extraction_notes: The paper does not apply machine learning methods; it performs a physical climate simulation study comparing global superparameterized simulations (HR-MMF) against idealized LES benchmarks from CGILS.
